questions.q: Why can ALTER INDEX ... REBUILD on a large table during business hours cause problems beyond the table being rebuilt?
options: It's fully logged and generates a large volume of transaction log that competes with the application's own writes for log-drive I/O
REBUILD always takes the database offline entirely
REBUILD permanently disables the index being rebuilt
It has no impact on anything other than the specific table involved
questions.explain: The transaction log volume generated by a large rebuild is shared with everything else writing to that same log file.

questions.q: What does REBUILD WITH (ONLINE = ON) actually change about the operation?
options: It allows reads and writes to continue against the table for most of the operation, instead of a full table-level lock
It eliminates all transaction log generation during the rebuild
It makes the rebuild complete instantly regardless of table size
It removes the need for a schema-modification lock entirely
questions.explain: ONLINE = ON improves concurrency but still briefly takes a schema-modification lock and adds its own tempdb/log overhead via row versioning.

questions.q: Why is REORGANIZE often the safer default for an index in the 10-30% fragmentation range, beyond just being the 'documented' choice?
options: It's always online, works incrementally, can be interrupted with no rollback of completed work, and generates far less transaction log than a rebuild
REORGANIZE is always faster than REBUILD on every table regardless of size
REORGANIZE requires Enterprise edition, so it's inherently more capable
REORGANIZE eliminates the need to ever check fragmentation again
questions.explain: REORGANIZE's incremental, interruptible, low-log-volume nature makes it genuinely lower-risk during business hours.

questions.q: Before rebuilding an index in production, what should a DBA check first, per this lesson?
options: Current server load, transaction log headroom, and whether the work can wait for a maintenance window
Only the avg_fragmentation_in_percent value, nothing else
Whether the table has ever been backed up
The number of columns in the index's included-columns list
questions.explain: Reading server load, log headroom, and timing constraints is what turns a documented threshold into an actual go/no-go decision.

questions.q: Why can REBUILD WITH (ONLINE = ON) still cause a noticeable performance hit even though reads and writes continue throughout?
options: It still takes a brief schema-modification lock at the start and end, and adds tempdb/log overhead of its own from row versioning
ONLINE = ON is purely cosmetic and changes nothing about how the rebuild runs
It silently blocks all reads for the entire duration despite the name
It only works on indexes smaller than 1,000 pages
questions.explain: "Online" describes concurrency during the operation, not the resource cost of performing it.
